name: rotor-weathervane-35
note: FAMILY D1, THE WEATHERVANE / heliBlend TIE-BREAKER - the highest-value card in this batch, because it is the only one that DISCRIMINATES BETWEEN TWO CANDIDATE FIXES rather than confirming one. WHAT IS BEING DECIDED. LAW-LEDGER.md H7 is AttackHelo1's deterministic 1.5-2.4 deg standing pointing residual (replicate CV +/-1-3%), the corpus's first above-floor rotorcraft pointing measurement. It is now traced to the GAME's own HeloFlyByWire weathervane term, which adds a sideslip bias into the yaw RATE ERROR above yawWeathervaneMinSpeed = 40 m/s (decompile :36028-36034 and :36047-36052). The corpus agrees and cannot arbitrate: every CONVERGED R42 tag sits below 40 m/s (34.96, 18.18, 7.33) and every PARKED tag sits at 41.5-41.8 m/s, so 40 falls inside a 0.3 m/s gap at the bottom of a 20 m/s ramp - the split is real and the sample is a single point. TWO MODELS EXPLAIN IT AND THEY PREDICT OPPOSITE THINGS AT 60 m/s. (1) WEATHERVANE: the residual is the game's sideslip bias, it switches on at 40 m/s, and above it num2 saturates to 1.0, so at 60 m/s the residual should be ~13x the R42 value or the pedal should rail outright. (2) heliBLEND: the residual belongs to the mod's rotorcraft yaw path, which is faded out by heliBlend = clamp01((HeliForwardSpeed - vFwd)/(HeliForwardSpeed - HeliHoverSpeed)); at the shipped 60/20 pins, 60 m/s puts heliBlend at exactly 0, the BANK channel takes the whole turn demand, and the residual should DISAPPEAR. One card, two speeds, opposite predictions, no third outcome that fits both. THE SIGNAL is terminal |off| (and fixedWindowOffDeg) plotted against the capture's own spd column, never against the declared entry speed. 35 m/s arm: both models predict a small residual, 0.00-0.1 deg, and it is the control. 60 m/s arm: weathervane predicts >= 10-30 deg or a railed pedal (read stickRailPctY), heliBlend predicts ~0 with the bank channel carrying the turn (read tBankE and outR going live where they were dead in R42). READ spd FIRST OR READ NOTHING. The entry speed is WRITTEN by ScenarioForceEntry and nothing holds it (AuditHold is an instrument, not a controller), and on a rotorcraft the throttle is COLLECTIVE - it buys climb, not forward speed, which comes from attitude. R42 measured AttackHelo1 drifting 4.5 -> 38 m/s and then parking at 41.5-41.8 under TestDrone's own HoldThrottle 0.60, i.e. 0.60 converges just ABOVE the 40 m/s threshold. The pins below are cut from that one datum and ARE FIRST ESTIMATES: 0.45 to sit clear below 40, 0.85 to sit clear above it. IF THE 35 m/s ARM SPENDS ITS SEGMENTS ABOVE 40, OR THE 60 m/s ARM BELOW 40, THE CARD MEASURED NOTHING - re-cut the pins from the spd column and re-fly. That failure mode is cheap to detect and is the first thing to check. startSpeed IS DECLARED > 0 ON PURPOSE. ScenarioPlayer.OwnInputs early-returns at EntrySpeed <= 0, which is exactly why rotor-bistab could not own its throttle and flew TestDrone's 0.60 for the whole card whatever it pinned. A positive entry speed is the only way a rotorcraft card gets its ScenarioThrottle pin honoured at all. IT ALSO CLOSES O14(c). None of the three R42 rotor cards declared an armToggle, so no 'arm=' appeared on any R42 '# config' line, 'arm=-1' could not appear, and the v1.0.1 warm-up fix (#55b) is code-reviewed rather than measured. This card carries Control/IntegralStallGate, which is a real lever here and not a token: the fine integrator winding on error PERSISTENCE instead of error MAGNITUDE is precisely the mechanism that should or should not erase a DETERMINISTIC STANDING residual. repeat 5 = one anchor (replicate 0, scored by neither arm per ledger X27) plus 2 scored replicates per arm per lane, x2 lanes = 4 per arm. GEOMETRY is rotor-bistab's shape at larger dwell: quiet at boresight, then two azimuth steps of increasing size, each bracketed by a return to boresight so the next step is measured from quiet rather than chained off the previous one. 40 s legs because the readout is a STANDING residual and needs to settle, not a transient. ROSTER: AttackHelo1 is H7's own airframe; UtilityHelo1 is the compound helo and has never been flown by this project at all (AIRFRAMES.md has no measured FBW corner for it). If the residual is the game's weathervane term it must appear on both; if it appears on AttackHelo1 alone it is not the game's shared HeloFlyByWire and both models are wrong. QuadVTOL1 is deliberately absent - it is a tiltwing and belongs to D2. THIS CARD IS WHY NO CODE SHIPS TONIGHT: it decides whether the fix goes into the mod's yaw path (heliBlend model) or into a sideslip compensation against the game's own term (weathervane model), and those are different one-line changes in different files. THIS ARM: 35 m/s, BELOW yawWeathervaneMinSpeed = 40. The weathervane term is OFF and heliBlend is 0.625 at the shipped 60/20 pins, i.e. the mod's rotorcraft yaw path is mostly live. BOTH MODELS PREDICT A SMALL RESIDUAL HERE (0.00-0.1 deg): this arm is the control that makes the 60 m/s arm readable, and it is also the arm that reproduces R42's converged tags (34.96 m/s) at a declared rather than accidental speed. A LARGE residual here refutes both models at once and sends the search back to the mod's own hover-yaw gains.
